block_calculation.cone: C=[[A,-B^dagger],[-B,D]] with D invertible and G=D^-1
block_calculation.right: psi=(x,y), y=G Bx, and (A-B^dagger G B)x=0
block_calculation.left: phi=(alpha,beta), beta=alpha B^dagger G, and alpha(A-B^dagger G B)=0
block_calculation.qualification: for non-selfadjoint parameter families the displayed left formulas use the appropriate transpose/dual products, not an unlicensed same-Hilbert-space adjoint

forcing_variation.cofactor_pairing: <phi,dot C_f psi>=-alpha(dot B_f^dagger y)-beta(dot B_f x)
forcing_variation.selfadjoint_seam: if phi is the Green/Riesz dual of psi and dot B_f x=f, this becomes the oriented two-sided forcing pairing, conventionally -2 Re<y,f>
forcing_variation.meaning: the determinant cofactor and Green forcing row coincide automatically only after a valid duality identification of left and right states

reciprocal_correction.natural_law: the source construction is reciprocal, so the expected operator relation is C(s)^dagger conjugate to C(1-conjugate(s)), not C(s)^dagger=C(s) for arbitrary s
reciprocal_correction.left_state: a left kernel covector at s is naturally transported from a right kernel state at 1-conjugate(s)
reciprocal_correction.consequence: off the critical seam, determinant cofactors pair two reciprocal states; they do not canonically identify a state with its own positive Green dual
reciprocal_correction.on_seam: s=1-conjugate(s) only when Re(s)=1/2, where the reciprocal pair can become one self-dual state

noncircular_form.wrong: assume same-state selfadjointness at an Xi zero and infer it lies on the seam
noncircular_form.right: retain psi_s and psi_(1-conjugate(s)) as two independently transported states, derive their relative Green identity, and show the alternating boundary vanishes
noncircular_form.confinement: if the boundary is independently zero and E_rel is strictly positive/nonzero, then Re(s)=1/2

orientation_obstruction.Fourier_fact: the direct and reciprocal corona limits have the same sign
orientation_obstruction.therefore: Fourier sewing alone adds rather than cancels their Green boundaries
orientation_obstruction.needed: a source-derived Cech/mapping-cone incidence delta(a,b)=a-F^-1 b supplies the alternating sign
orientation_obstruction.effect: this incidence is part of the missing R-D-G triangle, not a consequence of determinant or reciprocal symmetry

higher_coherence_reading: The triangle must compare a determinant cofactor built from right/left reciprocal kernel towers with a Green boundary built from the same two towers and an independently oriented relative incidence. The top tetrahedral mate can only be formed after this two-state triangle commutes.
next_iteration: Build the abstract two-state complex K_s direct-sum K_(1-conjugate(s)) with diagonal positive energy and Cech differential (1,-F^-1). Compute its Green boundary and identify exactly which term must equal the cofactor variation. Check whether the existing endpoint C4/Clifford block supplies the required alternating incidence without reusing Stokes cancellation.
iteration_result: The finite Schur computation shows that the missing determinant covector is naturally the reciprocal left state. Same-state cofactor/Green equality is valid only on the seam and cannot be assumed. The noncircular missing coherence is a two-state reciprocal Green identity with independently sourced alternating incidence.
